learning_objective: 🎯 Let us discover special prepositions that show movement and direction from one place to another!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Across means moving from one side to the other over a surface. Through means moving inside something like a dark tunnel or a thick forest!
Into shows movement entering inside something (jumping into the pool). Onto shows movement landing on top of something (jumping onto the bed).
Towards means moving in the direction of something. Along means moving in a line next to something, like walking along the river.

fun_activity.title: 🧭 The Movement Game
fun_activity.instructions: Walk 'towards' the door, step 'onto' a small mat, and pretend to swim 'through' a magical tunnel!

quick_recap: ⭐ Prepositions of direction show us exactly where someone or something is moving.
⭐ We use 'into' for going inside a place and 'onto' for getting on top of a surface.
⭐ 'Through' is for going inside something and coming out the other side!
